title: The per-site app shell is deployed by the account pipeline
description:
For a deployment such as Humorus, the app-shell CDK stack (Amplify CMS app, roles, edge) is deployed from Git on merge, not by a person running cdk deploy. The Amplify GitHub connection and the Google OAuth client are the person-only parts. Plan in the comments.

```gherkin
Feature: The app shell is deployed by the account pipeline

  Scenario: A merge to main deploys the app shell
    Given a deployment repository with infra/site.json
    When a change is merged to main
    Then the pipeline synthesizes the app-shell stack without AWS access
    And it asserts the manifest holds exactly the expected stack
    And it deploys it with the main-only deploy role through the CDK bootstrap roles
    And the stack output with the CMS app id is available to later steps

  Scenario: A pull request never needs AWS access to be checked
    Given a pull request that changes infra/site.json
    When CI runs
    Then the stack is synthesized and checked with no AWS credentials

  Scenario: The CMS never takes the public apex
    Given a site whose public domain is served by another stack
    When the app shell is deployed without a domain name
    Then the CMS is served on the Amplify default URL only

comments.author: home
comments.text:
# Plan: the per-site app shell (TheHallucinator.ai) deployed by the account pipeline

Planning only. Evidence is in Papyrus at origin/develop as of 2026-11-11. Nothing is built yet. infra/amplify-app-shell/ needs NO edits for the walking skeleton (see 6).

## 1. What a deployment repo must contain for the CMS app to build
Modelled on Distinctive-web and docs/standard-site.md: `package.json` pinning `@anthusai/papyrus` (plus @aws-amplify/backend, backend-cli, seed, aws-cdk-lib, constructs, next, react, react-dom, zod) with `papyrus-app sync && next build`, `package-lock.json`, `papyrus.config.ts` (defineSite with brands, defaultBrand, backend: brandId, auth, publication, features), `publication/brand.ts` and `theme.css`, `amplify/backend.ts` and `amplify/data/resource.ts` (one-line re-exports of `@anthusai/papyrus/backend`), `next.config.mjs` (withPapyrus), `middleware.ts`, `tsconfig.json`, `papyrus-modules.d.ts`, `requirements-publication.txt` (`papyrus-newsroom==<same version>`) and `infra/site.json`. No `amplify.yml`: the shell sets the build spec on the app. Missing in Papyrus: there is no scaffold command (`papyrus-app` offers sync, brand diff, alexa-sync, videoml-bundle), so the skeleton copies the Distinctive layout by hand; HUM-4bca14 is the Papyrus work. Suggested `site.json`: `frontend: pretext` (a markus-static site needs Python hook code, against Humorus rule 2; unverified that pretext builds with no extra code), stackName `humorus-app-shell`, `aws.region` only (the account comes from `PAPYRUS_AWS_ACCOUNT_ID`, set from the repository variable), `cms.staging: false`, no domainName or hostedZoneId (so the CMS cannot touch the apex: it serves on the Amplify default URL, which the stack appends to the redirect list), `github` owner, repo and the numeric ownerId/repoId (needed for the immutable OIDC subject), `cms.cognitoDomainPrefix` with `applyCognitoDomainPrefix: true`, `cms.environment.PAPYRUS_OAUTH_REDIRECT_URLS` (http://localhost:3001/ required) and `PAPYRUS_TENANT_ID`.

## 2. Deploy mechanism
A new reusable workflow `app-shell-deploy.yml` (same inputs as account-stacks.yml): job synth with no AWS credentials (`npm ci`, `papyrus-infra synth --site infra/site.json --out cdk.out`, assert the manifest holds exactly the one expected stack, upload the artifact); on push to main, a deploy job as the main-only deploy role runs `cdk deploy --app cdk.out --require-approval never` (pinned aws-cdk) and reads the `CmsAppId` output; then the existing amplify-deploy.yml with the `<siteId>-github-deploy` role the shell creates.
Roles added to `infra/account/baseline.yaml`: parameter `CdkQualifier` (default hnb659fds); on the deploy role `sts:AssumeRole` and `sts:TagSession` on the CDK deploy and file-publishing roles (not image-publishing); on the plan role the lookup role only if a diff is wanted. The CDK roles trust the account root, so the identity-policy allow is enough.
Plain English: a push to main can now run any CloudFormation change as the CDK execution role, which is AdministratorAccess unless the bootstrap set CloudFormationExecutionPolicies (the live CDKToolkit parameters are unread: the SSO token expired; Ryan can read them after `aws sso login`). The baseline's explicit deny on the baseline stack does not bind CDK. In practice this adds little power: the CMS service role is already AdministratorAccess and the Amplify build runs main's code as that role. Safety is the same as today: main-only trust, branch protection with `ci`, pinned workflow. Not covered: the deployer's Replace/Remove refusal does not apply to cdk deploy (a follow-up can run CDK with `--method prepare-change-set` and check it). PRs run synth plus the manifest assertion with no AWS credentials (a `cdk diff` would need the lookup role, which is read-only for nearly the whole account; add later if wanted). CDKToolkit stays hand-made.

## 3. The Amplify GitHub connection
`AWS::Amplify::App` accepts `Repository` plus `AccessToken` ("used to authorize access to a GitHub repository using the Amplify GitHub App", not stored). The Amplify GitHub App must still be installed on the repo (a GitHub-side step by an organisation admin). Whether `{{resolve:ssm-secure:...}}` works for AccessToken is unverified. The robust codifiable route is a NoEcho CfnParameter for AccessToken, the deploy job reading a SecureString with `ssm get-parameter --with-decryption` and passing `cdk deploy --parameters`: that touches lib/amplify-app-shell.ts and lib/site-config.ts and adds a deploy-role grant on one named parameter. Today the code supports a Secrets Manager secret, which conflicts with the SSM-over-Secrets-Manager rule. Recommendation for the skeleton: the one-time console connect (docs/site-hosting.md), codify the token later. Person-only: installing the AWS Amplify GitHub App on the repo, and either the console connect or creating a PAT and putting it in SSM. Unknown: whether a later CloudFormation update drops a console-made connection when Repository is absent from the template; read the first change set.

## 4. Google sign-in (what Ryan creates)
In Google Cloud Console: a project for this site; an OAuth consent screen (External unless all editors share an organisation; add editors as test users while in Testing); scopes openid, email, profile; a Web application OAuth client with Authorized JavaScript origin `https://<prefix>.auth.us-east-1.amazoncognito.com` and Authorized redirect URI that origin plus `/oauth2/idpresponse`. Do not add the CMS URL or localhost to Google. Suggested Cognito prefix: `papyrus-the-hallucinator` (lowercase, unique in the region, no aws/amazon/cognito); set it with applyCognitoDomainPrefix true before the first backend build so the URIs are known up front. The secrets go to SSM SecureStrings at `/amplify/<appId>/main-branch-<hash>/GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` and `.../GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET`, written by Ryan running `papyrus site google-secrets set` from the Humorus checkout (needs the CmsAppId from the first deploy and PAPYRUS_AWS_ACCOUNT_ID); agents may run `check`. Then rebuild main. After the first sign-in a person adds the editor to the Cognito group (admin, editor or curator).

## 5. Tenant id
`PAPYRUS_TENANT_ID` is a build variable (`^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,62}$`, so `the-hallucinator` works), settable in `cms.environment`, passed to five Lambdas. Item, PublishedItem, MediaAsset, PublishedMediaAsset and NewsroomSection get a tenantId and tenant-prefixed index keys; about 50 other models (including Reference) get only an optional tenantId stamped by a tenant client. The Tenant, TenantMembership and TenantDomain tables exist but "nothing reads or writes them yet". Gap: a Reference carrying the tenant id is not proven for browser-side writes from the newsroom UI. Set the id in the first deploy; earlier rows are bare.

## 6. Files to touch and order
infra/amplify-app-shell: none for the skeleton (the PAT route later: lib/amplify-app-shell.ts, lib/site-config.ts). Papyrus: infra/account/baseline.yaml, the new app-shell-deploy.yml, a manifest-check script under infra/pipeline/, docs, a Gherkin feature, a PPY issue for the scaffold command. Humorus: the site files, infra/site.json, a caller workflow, a bump of the Papyrus pin.
Order: (1) Ryan signs in and reads the CDKToolkit parameters; (2) Papyrus PR (baseline, workflow, docs, feature); (3) Humorus PR (site files, site.json, workflow, pin bump), the roles job applies the baseline with no person; (4) Ryan installs the Amplify GitHub App and does the Google setup; (5) merge to main, deploy outputs CmsAppId; (6) Ryan does the console connect and `google-secrets set`; (7) first Amplify build with PAPYRUS_BOOTSTRAP_STAGE=1 (about 13 minutes), then a PR removing the variable and a second build; (8) add the editor to the group and test sign-in. Estimate 2 to 3 working days elapsed, mostly waiting on Ryan.
Risks: the live CDKToolkit roles and version; the pending Lambda concurrency increase (10 to 1,000) and the AppSync 429 problem on new accounts; the two-deploy backend; whether pretext builds with no extra code; inspect the synthesized Amplify Domain before enabling newsroom.thehallucinator.ai so it cannot claim the apex the placeholder owns; the console connection surviving later updates.

comments.text: Decision update 2026-11-12: Ryan rejected any long-lived GitHub token and any hand step. Finding: Machines on Machines works as follows (read-only): the stack creates the Amplify app with NO repository; the app is connected once in the console by an administrator authorizing the Amplify GitHub App (repositoryCloneMethod TOKEN: Amplify holds the installation access, we hold nothing); autoBuild off, no webhooks; each deploy is an OIDC StartJob RELEASE with the commit id. So the one hand step is the connection (an authorization). AWS says Amplify Hosting does not support manual deploys for SSR apps, so a Git-less route is unavailable; the token-free alternative to spike is a CodeCommit mirror. PAT-in-SSM plan removed. Build: PR 1412 (no change to infra/amplify-app-shell).
